# Judith Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_010_page_001.jpg

---

**10:1** When the last word of her prayer had left her lips,

**10:2** Judith rose from the floor. She called her maid, went down into the house, stripped off the sackcloth, and shed her widow's clothes.

**10:3** She washed herself clean. She rubbed rich myrrh into her skin. She braided her hair and set a tiara on her head. She put on the beautiful clothes she had worn when her husband Manasseh was alive.

**10:4** She buckled her sandals. She put on ankle-rings, bracelets, rings, earrings, every piece of jewelry she owned — and made herself as beautiful as she knew how. She was arming herself. Her beauty was her weapon. Every ornament was calculated to catch the eye of any man who saw her.

**10:5** She loaded her maid with provisions: a skin of wine, a flask of oil, a bag of roasted grain, dried fig cakes, fine bread — all of it wrapped and packed.

**10:6** They walked to the city gate. Uzziah was there waiting with the two elders, Chabris and Charmis.

**10:7** When they looked at her, they stopped. Her face was different. Her clothes were different. The transformation stunned them. They stood there, overcome by her beauty, and said:

**10:8** "May the God of our ancestors give you his grace and see your plan through — for the glory of Israel, for the honor of Jerusalem." Judith bowed her head before God.

**10:9** "Open the gate," she said. The elders gave the order and the guards opened it.

**10:10** Judith went through — her maid behind her. The men of the city watched them go, watched them descend the slope, cross the valley, and finally disappear from sight.

**10:11** In the valley below, an Assyrian patrol spotted them.

**10:12** The soldiers grabbed her. "Who are you? Where are you from? Where are you going?" "I am a Hebrew woman," she said. "I am running away from my own people because they are about to be handed over to you.

**10:13** I am on my way to Holofernes — your commander. I have intelligence for him. I can show him the exact route to take the whole hill country without losing a single man."

**10:14** The soldiers listened. Then they looked at her face. She was stunning — a beauty beyond anything they had seen. They said:

**10:15** "You just saved your life by coming down here yourself. Now go to his tent. We will escort you personally until you are standing in front of him.

**10:16** Do not be afraid when you face him. Tell him what you told us and he will treat you well."

**10:17** A hundred men formed up around her and her maid and marched them to the tent of Holofernes.

**10:18** Word flew through the camp. Tent to tent — a woman had come in. Soldiers poured out to see her, crowding around while she stood outside Holofernes' tent waiting to be announced.

**10:19** They stared. And the longer they stared, the more they marveled — not just at her, but at Israel. A people that could produce a woman like this? Man after man turned to his neighbor: "Who could ever write off a nation with women like that? Leave one man alive and they will outsmart the whole world."

**10:20** Holofernes' personal guard and all his attendants came out and brought her inside the tent.

**10:21** Holofernes himself was stretched out on his bed beneath a canopy — purple and gold, studded with emeralds and precious stones.

**10:22** They announced her. He came out into the anteroom, silver lamps blazing ahead of him.

**10:23** Judith stepped before him. His entire staff stared at her face — the sheer beauty of it was a blow. She dropped to the ground before him in a prostration. His servants lifted her back to her feet.
